oneLineDefinition: A field that extracts actionable insights from data using statistics, programming, and domain knowledge to support business decisions.
overview: Data Science sits at the intersection of statistics, programming, and business understanding. Unlike AI which emphasizes model building, Data Science emphasizes understanding data patterns, communicating findings, and supporting decisions. Students learn SQL, Python, statistics, and data visualization. Roles vary widely — from purely analytical (dashboards, reports) to more technical (building ML pipelines). It is generally less mathematically intense than AI but requires strong statistical intuition.
typicalProjects: Build a sales performance dashboard for a retail company
Analyze user churn patterns and identify at-risk segments
Design and analyze an A/B test for a product feature
Build a demand forecasting model using historical data
Clean and merge data from multiple inconsistent sources
requiredSkills: Statistical thinking — understanding what a number actually means
SQL fluency for data extraction and transformation
Data storytelling — presenting findings to non-technical stakeholders
Critical thinking about data quality and sampling bias
Python for data manipulation and basic modeling
suitableFor: Students who like finding patterns and explaining 'why' behind numbers
Those who enjoy combining technical work with communication
People interested in business, product, or policy — not just pure engineering
Students who are good at statistics but prefer applied over theoretical math
notSuitableFor: Those who want to avoid statistics entirely
Students who only want to build software products
People who dislike presenting or explaining findings to others
keyTakeaways: Most of the job is cleaning and questioning data, not running models
SQL is often more useful day-to-day than Python in analyst roles
Communication skills matter as much as technical skills
Data Science roles vary enormously across companies — always check the actual job description
cautionNotes: 'Data Scientist' titles at different companies can mean very different things — from BI analyst to ML engineer
Many 'Data Science' programs in Vietnam focus heavily on AI/ML and may underemphasize SQL and business analytics
Entry-level roles often involve more reporting than modeling
careerPaths: Machine Learning Engineer (with additional ML depth)
marketDemand: Consistently high across industries — finance, e-commerce, logistics, healthcare, and government all hire data roles. Analyst roles are more abundant than scientist roles.
salaryOutlook: Data Analysts in Vietnam earn 12–20M VND/month at entry level. Data Scientists with ML skills can earn 20–40M+. Senior roles at product companies or international firms pay significantly more.
futureTrend: Growth in demand for data roles that combine technical skill with business acumen. SQL and data engineering skills are increasingly valued. AI tools are automating some basic analysis, raising the bar for analyst roles.
commonMisconceptions: Data Science is the same as AI — Data Science is broader and more business-oriented
You need to know machine learning to be a data analyst — many analyst roles primarily use SQL and Excel
Data Science is just about building dashboards — senior roles involve experimental design, modeling, and strategy

faq.question: What is the difference between Data Science and AI?
faq.answer: Data Science focuses on extracting insights from data and communicating them to support decisions. AI focuses on building systems that learn and make predictions autonomously. They overlap in machine learning but have different emphases and career paths.

faq.question: Do I need to be good at math to study Data Science?
faq.answer: You need solid statistics and some calculus, but it is less mathematically intensive than AI. Strong statistical intuition and SQL fluency matter more than advanced calculus.
